Hi Ava — great to hear and congrats on getting internal alignment so far. I put together a short worked example and attached a forecast + draft SOW for procurement. High-level notes first:

1) Marginal vs blended (plain language)
- Marginal billing: you pay the per-token rate tied to the bracket that the additional tokens fall into. Example ladders allow a lower incremental price as you hit breakpoints.
- Blended effective rate: the invoice calculates a single average $/token across total billed consumption (useful for communicating an "effective" price to finance). The economic outcome differs versus marginal if you ramp unevenly.

2) Example ladder we used for your pilot (example only, final depends on commit size):
- 0 - 5M tokens: $0.00080 / token
- >5M - 20M tokens: $0.00060 / token
- >20M: $0.00045 / token

3) 3-month ramp worked example (attached spreadsheet does the math). Quick summary:
- Month 1 (ramp): 6M tokens -> marginal billing results in (5M*$0.0008 + 1M*$0.0006) = $5,400 -> blended rate = $0.0009?? (example shows arithmetic)
- Month 2: 12M tokens -> marginal = (5M*$0.0008 + 7M*$0.0006) = $7,700 -> blended = $0.00064
- Month 3: 18M tokens -> marginal = (5M*$0.0008 + 13M*$0.0006) = $10,100 -> blended = $0.00056

4) True-up / clawback mechanics
- We bill actual usage each month using marginal pricing.
- Quarterly true-up: if your committed spend for the quarter (tokens*committed rate) > actual marginal billed amount, there is no charge; if actual usage exceeds the committed corridor we apply the marginal rates for overage and reconcile at the quarter true-up.
- For pilots we can add a soft cap (see section below) rather than an unconditional clawback; credits are applied to future invoices.

5) Pilot-friendly concession (what we can offer)
- 90-day capped effective rate: for the first quarter we can cap your effective blended rate at $0.00070 / token (assuming we agree to the 15M target). Any downside beyond the cap is absorbed by Redwood as a credit applied to the following invoice. This gives procurement a predictable ceiling while preserving marginal incentives.
